identity.question: Will Dolly Parton be the #1 searched passing on Google this year?

operative_rule: Named winner must be #1 in Google official Year in Search Global → Trending → Passings for 2026. Settlement uses the specified list, regardless of navigation. If Google does not release the specified 2026 list by 2027-03-31 23:59 ET, market resolves Other. This differs from total search volume and from a generic weekly Google Trends peak.

facts.claim: Official Dolly Parton site published an announcement dated 2026-08-25 stating she died that day in Nashville at age 80; the article names her music, acting, philanthropy, writing and other public roles.
The exact official Global 2026 Year in Search route returned HTTP 404; this documents that route response only and does not establish that no 2026 list exists on another route or will be published.

The 2025 official method defines Year in Search trends by fastest increase in search interest/traffic against the same period of the prior year using Google Trends plus internal tools; it is not absolute or total search volume. The retained method is explicitly about 2025; its exact cutoff/formula cannot be transferred as an established 2026 fact.

A prior official Google Trends comparison requested Jan 1–Oct 17, 2026, worldwide/global, category 0, web search, with Chuck Norris, Alex Pretti, Kevin Keegan, Franco Baresi and Dolly Parton. It returned HTTP 429, no values; this is an access gap, not zero interest or a ranking.
facts.scope: Official Trends query: Global geography, category 0, web search; five named terms including Dolly; 2026-01-01 through 2026-10-17. Query/term list and request details retained in linked source packet.
